note: CBS News (2008-05-22): the $15M fourth round was led by Fidelity Ventures with 'past backers' Bessemer, Catamount and Shasta taking part, and the three earlier rounds were never announced in detail; no source read names the round Bessemer entered in 2005.

Wikipedia's Z-Wave article: 'In 2005, Bessemer Venture Partners led a $16 million third seed round for Zensys'. A $16M third round of a company founded in 1999 is read as a later round (Growth), not as a seed, whatever the article's wording.

AVEO's S-1: 'On March 26, 2007, April 10, 2007 and April 27, 2007, we sold an aggregate of 21,165,510 shares of our series D convertible preferred stock'. The firm's own investment date is 2007-04-10, the second close, and Bessemer Venture Partners VI Institutional signs the investor rights agreement filed with the S-1, so the entry was the Series D (Growth). The S-1's holder table lists only 5% holders and does not name Bessemer.

Soap.com is a Quidsi site, so this row is the same company and investment as quidsi-fka-diapers-com and diapers-com. TechCrunch (2008-10-03): Diapers.com 'raised a $7 million round led by Bessemer Venture Partners in 2007', then a larger Accel round; TechCrunch (2010-04-20) calls the October 2009 round the Series E. No page read gives the 2007 round its letter; it is taken as the Series B (Growth), which a vendor profile also says, since the company already had venture backers (MentorTech, BEV Capital) by then.

A June 2016 release describes 'Los Angeles-based Onestop Internet ... backed by blue-chip investors Bessemer Ventures and Fung Capital USA' (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/linens-n-things-launches-new-ecommerce-platform-with-onestop-internet-300284761.html). Its fate after 2018 and the 2008 round's name were not found (two news queries).

Wikipedia: QuinStreet acquired the media assets of Ziff Davis Enterprise, including eWeek, in February 2012 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuinStreet), so acquired. Insight Venture Partners had bought the division from Ziff Davis Media in July 2007; no source read says whether Bessemer was part of that buying group (a control ruling candidate) or which round its 2008 investment was.

Still listed on the NSE and BSE in 2026: share price and shareholding pages are current, and the company announced a third interim distribution to its debenture holders in April 2026 (https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/il-fs-transportation-networks-announces-third-interim-distribution-to-non-convertible-debenture-holders/37791810) under the IL&FS group resolution that has run since 2018. No sale or delisting was found, so the row reads public, far below $1B.

An insolvency process against the company (the NCLAT ruling Palogix Infrastructure v. ICICI Bank is its best known trace) ended in a resolution plan under which Sanjay Kumar Mishra (JFC Finance) acquired it, with creditors recovering Rs 56.84 crore of Rs 154.39 crore claimed (https://insolvencytracker.in/2021/03/07/how-women-insolvency-professionals-have-fared-in-ibc-an-analysis-in-numbers/): a sale out of insolvency, so acquired. Kolkata from knowledge. The 2010 round is not named.

TechCrunch (2012-05-14): 'a Series A round of $4.5 million' led by Atlas Venture with NextView 'and new investors Bessemer Venture Partners and Salesforce.com'. The firm's own date, 2011-12-02, is kept as the entry date. Mediafly announced it would acquire Boston-based InsightSquared in December 2021 (https://www.builtinchicago.org/articles/mediafly-to-acquire-boston-insightqquared-hiring).

VC News Daily (2012-11-13): Xtime 'raised $23 million in Series 2 funding ... led by Bessemer Venture Partners with participation from Lumia Capital and existing investors RPM Ventures and Saints Capital'. A second series into a company founded in 1999 with existing venture holders is a later round (Growth). The same page places Xtime in Redwood Shores, which is Redwood City.

Graduated: TechCrunch (2014-03-18), 'Nitrous.IO Closes $6.65M Series A Round Led By Bessemer'. The company announced on 2016-10-31 that it was shutting the service down on November 14 (https://techcrunch.com/2016/10/31/cloud-development-platform-nitrous-io-shuts-down/), so defunct. San Francisco from knowledge (the founders moved from Singapore).

BetaKit (2015-01-14): the $18M Series B 'is led by Bessemer Venture Partners with participation from existing investors', and Byron Deeter joined the board; the firm's own date is 2014-12-03. Bessemer was not in the 2013 Series A, so the entry is Growth. TechCrunch calls Vidyard 'a Kitchener, Ontario-based company', which confirms Canada.

Entered at the $30M Series C that Bessemer led, announced in January 2015 (from knowledge; two news queries returned no page naming the round). The firm's 2014 date is a year-end placeholder for that close.

KnowMe was the New York company of filmmaker Andrew Jarecki (headlines in Inc. and Inverse, early 2016; city from knowledge). What became of it after 2016 and the round Bessemer entered were not found.

This row is the same company as wildlife-studios and is aligned to it (Sao Paulo, per Crunchbase News; $3B mark of August 2020, older than 24 months; the firm's 2012 year). The two rows should be merged. The 2012 round is not named.
